text: Definition 2.1 (NC–C function classes) . Given $L,D_{\mathcal{Y}}>0$ , consider continuously differentiable functions $f:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}$ , over all finite dimensions $d_{x},d_{y}\in\mathbb{N}$ , where $\mathcal{X}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}}$ and $\mathcal{Y}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}$ are nonempty closed convex sets with $0\in\mathcal{X}$ and $0\in\mathcal{Y}$ , satisfying: 1. $f$ is jointly $L$ -smooth on $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ : $\|\nabla f(\bm{x},\bm{y})-\nabla f(\bm{x}^{\prime},\bm{y}^{\prime})\|\leq L\|(\bm{x},\bm{y})-(\bm{x}^{\prime},\bm{y}^{\prime})\|,\qquad\forall(\bm{x},\bm{y}),(\bm{x}^{\prime},\bm{y}^{\prime})\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}.$ 2. For every $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$ , $f(\bm{x},\cdot)$ is concave. 3. The dual domain satisfies: $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{Y}):=\sup_{\bm{y},\bm{y}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\|\bm{y}-\bm{y}^{\prime}\|\leq D_{\mathcal{Y}}$ . 4. The initial scale is parameterized in either of the following two ways: (i) For $\Delta_{\Phi}>0$ , $\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}(L,\Delta_{\Phi},D_{\mathcal{Y}})$ denotes the class of functions satisfying $\Phi_{f}(\bm{0})-\inf_{\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}}\Phi_{f}(\bm{x})\leq\Delta_{\Phi};$ (ii) For $\mathcal{G}_{0}>0$ , $\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}^{\rm pd}(L,\mathcal{G}_{0},D_{\mathcal{Y}})$ denotes the class of functions satisfying $\max_{\bm{y}\in\mathcal{Y}}f(0,\bm{y})-\inf_{\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}}f(\bm{x},0)\leq\mathcal{G}_{0}.$

Definition 2.3 . Let $f\in\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}(L,\Delta_{\Phi},D_{\mathcal{Y}})\cup\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}^{\rm pd}(L,\mathcal{G}_{0},D_{\mathcal{Y}})$ . A point $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$ is $\epsilon$ -stationary for the primal value function if $\left\lVert\nabla(\varphi_{f})_{1/(2L)}(\bm{x})\right\rVert\leq\epsilon.$ A random output $\bm{x}$ is expected $\epsilon$ -stationary if $\mathbb{E}\left\lVert\nabla(\varphi_{f})_{1/(2L)}(\bm{x})\right\rVert\leq\epsilon.$

Definition 2.4 (Deterministic first-order oracle) . The deterministic first-order oracle of a differentiable function $f:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is the mapping $\mathcal{O}_{f}^{\rm fo}(\bm{x},\bm{y})=(f(\bm{x},\bm{y}),\nabla_{\bm{x}}f(\bm{x},\bm{y}),\nabla_{\bm{y}}f(\bm{x},\bm{y})),\qquad(\bm{x},\bm{y})\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}.$

Definition 2.7 (Zero-chain) . A differentiable function $f:\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a first-order zero-chain if, for every $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$ , $\operatorname{prog}_{0}(\nabla f(\bm{x}))\leq\min\{\operatorname{prog}_{0}(\bm{x})+1,d\}.$

Theorem 4.1 (Deterministic zero-respecting lower bound) . There exist universal constants $c_{0},c_{1}>0$ such that, for every $L,\Delta_{\Phi},D_{\mathcal{Y}}>0$ and every $\epsilon$ satisfying $0<\epsilon\leq c_{1}\min\{\sqrt{L\Delta_{\Phi}},\,LD_{\mathcal{Y}}\},$ (31) there is an instance $f\in\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}(L,\Delta_{\Phi},D_{\mathcal{Y}})$ on finite-dimensional closed convex sets $X_{0},Y_{0}$ , with $\operatorname{diam}(Y_{0})=D_{\mathcal{Y}}$ , for which the following lower bound holds. Let $\Phi(\bm{x}):=\max_{\bm{y}\in Y_{0}}f(\bm{x},\bm{y})$ and $\varphi:=\Phi+\iota_{X_{0}}$ . For any deterministic zero-respecting first-order algorithm, every zero-respecting primal output $\bm{x}\in X_{0}$ produced after $q$ joint oracle calls with $q<c_{0}L^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\Delta_{\Phi}\,\epsilon^{-3}$ (32) satisfies $\left\lVert\nabla\varphi_{1/(2L)}(\bm{x})\right\rVert=\left\lVert G_{1/(2L)}(\bm{x};\bm{p})\right\rVert>\epsilon,$ (33) where $\bm{p}$ is the unique point in $\mathcal{P}_{1/(2L)}(\bm{x})$ . Consequently, the deterministic zero-respecting first-order oracle complexity of finding an $\epsilon$ -stationary point is $\Omega\!\left(L^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\Delta_{\Phi}\,\epsilon^{-3}\right).$

Corollary 4.2 . There exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that, for every $L,\mathcal{G}_{0},D_{\mathcal{Y}}>0$ and every $\epsilon$ satisfying $0<\epsilon\leq c\min\{\sqrt{L\mathcal{G}_{0}},\,LD_{\mathcal{Y}}\},$ there is an instance $f\in\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}^{\rm pd}(L,\mathcal{G}_{0},D_{\mathcal{Y}})$ on which every deterministic zero-respecting first-order algorithm requires $\Omega\!\left(L^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\mathcal{G}_{0}\,\epsilon^{-3}\right)$ joint oracle evaluations to return an $\epsilon$ -stationary point of the primal value function.

Theorem 5.5 (Stochastic zero-respecting lower bound) . There exist universal constants $c_{\rm d},c_{\rm n},c_{1}>0$ such that, for every $L,\Delta_{\Phi},D_{\mathcal{Y}}>0$ , every $\sigma\geq 0$ , and every $\epsilon$ satisfying $0<\epsilon\leq c_{1}\min\{\sqrt{L\Delta_{\Phi}},\,LD_{\mathcal{Y}}\},$ (56) there is an instance $f^{\rm sg}\in\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}(L,\Delta_{\Phi},D_{\mathcal{Y}})$ on finite-dimensional closed convex sets $X_{0},Y_{0}$ , with $\operatorname{diam}(Y_{0})=D_{\mathcal{Y}}$ , equipped with an unbiased stochastic first-order oracle whose mean-square error is at most $\sigma^{2}$ . For this instance and oracle, every zero-respecting primal output $\bm{x}\in X_{0}$ produced by an adaptive stochastic zero-respecting algorithm after $q$ oracle calls with $q<c_{\rm d}L^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\Delta_{\Phi}\,\epsilon^{-3}+c_{\rm n}L^{3}D_{\mathcal{Y}}^{2}\Delta_{\Phi}\sigma^{2}\,\epsilon^{-6}$ (57) satisfies $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\lVert\nabla(\varphi_{\rm sg})_{1/(2L)}(\bm{x})\right\rVert\right]>\epsilon.$ (58) Consequently, finding an expected $\epsilon$ -stationary point requires $\Omega\!\left(L^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\Delta_{\Phi}\,\epsilon^{-3}+L^{3}D_{\mathcal{Y}}^{2}\Delta_{\Phi}\sigma^{2}\,\epsilon^{-6}\right)$ (59) stochastic first-order oracle evaluations.

Corollary 5.6 . There exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that, for every $L,\mathcal{G}_{0},D_{\mathcal{Y}}>0$ , every $\sigma\geq 0$ , and every $\epsilon$ satisfying $0<\epsilon\leq c\min\{\sqrt{L\mathcal{G}_{0}},LD_{\mathcal{Y}}\},$ there is an instance $f^{\rm sg}\in\mathcal{F}_{\rm NCC}^{\rm pd}(L,\mathcal{G}_{0},D_{\mathcal{Y}})$ equipped with a unbiased stochastic first-order oracle whose mean-square error is at most $\sigma^{2}$ , for which every adaptive stochastic zero-respecting algorithm requires $\Omega\!\left(L^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\mathcal{G}_{0}\,\epsilon^{-3}+L^{3}D_{\mathcal{Y}}^{2}\mathcal{G}_{0}\sigma^{2}\,\epsilon^{-6}\right)$ oracle calls to return an expected $\epsilon$ -stationary output.
